NKJV.1: Dead flies putrefy the perfumer’s ointment, And cause it to give off a foul odor; So does a little folly to one respected for wisdom and honor.
NKJV.2: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, But a fool’s heart at his left.
NKJV.3: Even when a fool walks along the way, He lacks wisdom, And he shows everyone that he is a fool.
NKJV.4: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you,  Do not leave your post; For conciliation pacifies great offenses.
NKJV.5: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, As an error proceeding from the ruler:
NKJV.6: Folly is set in great dignity, While the rich sit in a lowly place.
NKJV.7: I have seen servants on horses, While princes walk on the ground like servants.
NKJV.8: He who digs a pit will fall into it, And whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a serpent.
NKJV.9: He who quarries stones may be hurt by them, And he who splits wood may be endangered by it.
NKJV.10: If the ax is dull, And one does not sharpen the edge, Then he must use more strength; But wisdom brings success.
NKJV.11: A serpent may bite when it is not charmed; The babbler is no different.
NKJV.12: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, But the lips of a fool shall swallow him up;
NKJV.13: The words of his mouth begin with foolishness, And the end of his talk is raving madness.
NKJV.14: A fool also multiplies words. No man knows what is to be; Who can tell him what will be after him?
NKJV.15: The labor of fools wearies them, For they do not even know how to go to the city!
NKJV.16: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, And your princes feast in the morning!
NKJV.17: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, And your princes feast at the proper time— For strength and not for drunkenness!
NKJV.18: Because of laziness the building decays, And through idleness of hands the house leaks.
NKJV.19: A feast is made for laughter, And wine makes merry; But money answers everything.
NKJV.20: Do not curse the king, even in your thought; Do not curse the rich, even in your bedroom; For a bird of the air may carry your voice, And a bird in flight may tell the matter.

NASB.1: Dead flies make a perfumer's oil stink, so a little foolishness is weightier than wisdom [and] honor.
NASB.2: A wise man's heart [directs him] toward the right, but the foolish man's heart [directs him] toward the left.
NASB.3: Even when the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking and he demonstrates to everyone [that] he is a fool.
NASB.4: If the ruler's temper rises against you, do not abandon your position, because composure allays great offenses.
NASB.5: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like an error which goes forth from the ruler--
NASB.6: folly is set in many exalted places while rich men sit in humble places.
NASB.7: I have seen slaves [riding] on horses and princes walking like slaves on the land.
NASB.8: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and a serpent may bite him who breaks through a wall.
NASB.9: He who quarries stones may be hurt by them, and he who splits logs may be endangered by them.
NASB.10: If the axe is dull and he does not sharpen [its] edge, then he must exert more strength. Wisdom has the advantage of giving success.
NASB.11: If the serpent bites before being charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.
NASB.12: Words from the mouth of a wise man are gracious, while the lips of a fool consume him;
NASB.13: the beginning of his talking is folly and the end of it is wicked madness.
NASB.14: Yet the fool multiplies words. No man knows what will happen, and who can tell him what will come after him?
NASB.15: The toil of a fool [so] wearies him that he does not [even] know how to go to a city.
NASB.16: Woe to you, O land, whose king is a lad and whose princes feast in the morning.
NASB.17: Blessed are you, O land, whose king is of nobility and whose princes eat at the appropriate time-- for strength and not for drunkenness.
NASB.18: Through indolence the rafters sag, and through slackness the house leaks.
NASB.19: [Men] prepare a meal for enjoyment, and wine makes life merry, and money is the answer to everything.
NASB.20: Furthermore, in your bedchamber do not curse a king, and in your sleeping rooms do not curse a rich man, for a bird of the heavens will carry the sound and the winged creature will make the matter known.

NLT.1:
As dead flies cause even a bottle of perfume to stink,
so a little foolishness spoils great wisdom and honor.
NLT.2:
A wise person chooses the right road;
a fool takes the wrong one.
NLT.3:
You can identify fools
just by the way they walk down the street!
NLT.4:
If your boss is angry at you, don’t quit!
A quiet spirit can overcome even great mistakes.
NLT.5: There is another evil I have seen under the sun. Kings and rulers make a grave mistake
NLT.6: when they give great authority to foolish people and low positions to people of proven worth.
NLT.7: I have even seen servants riding horseback like princes — and princes walking like servants!
NLT.8:
When you dig a well,
you might fall in.
When you demolish an old wall,
you could be bitten by a snake.
NLT.9:
When you work in a quarry,
stones might fall and crush you.
When you chop wood,
there is danger with each stroke of your ax.
NLT.10:
Using a dull ax requires great strength,
so sharpen the blade.
That’s the value of wisdom;
it helps you succeed.
NLT.11:
If a snake bites before you charm it,
what’s the use of being a snake charmer?
NLT.12:
Wise words bring approval,
but fools are destroyed by their own words.
NLT.13:
Fools base their thoughts on foolish assumptions,
so their conclusions will be wicked madness;
NLT.14:
they chatter on and on.
No one really knows what is going to happen;
no one can predict the future.
NLT.15:
Fools are so exhausted by a little work
that they can’t even find their way home.
NLT.16:
What sorrow for the land ruled by a servant,
the land whose leaders feast in the morning.
NLT.17:
Happy is the land whose king is a noble leader
and whose leaders feast at the proper time
to gain strength for their work, not to get drunk.
NLT.18:
Laziness leads to a sagging roof;
idleness leads to a leaky house.
NLT.19:
A party gives laughter,
wine gives happiness,
and money gives everything!
NLT.20:
Never make light of the king, even in your thoughts.
And don’t make fun of the powerful, even in your own bedroom.
For a little bird might deliver your message
and tell them what you said.

AMP.1: Dead flies make the oil of the perfumer give off a foul odor; so a little foolishness [in one who is esteemed] outweighs wisdom and honor.
AMP.2: A wise man's heart turns him toward the right [which is the way of blessing], but a fool's heart turns him toward the left [which is the way of condemnation].
AMP.3: Even when a fool walks along the road, his [common] sense and good judgment fail him and he demonstrates to everyone that he is a fool.
AMP.4: If the temper of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your post [showing resistance], because composure and calmness prevent great offenses.
AMP.5: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like an error which proceeds from the ruler—
AMP.6: folly is set in many exalted places and in great dignity while the rich sit in humble places.
AMP.7: I have seen slaves riding on horses and princes walking like slaves on the ground.
AMP.8: He who digs a pit [for others] may fall into it, and a serpent may bite him who breaks through a [stone] wall.
AMP.9: He who quarries stones may be hurt with them, and he who splits logs may be endangered by them.
AMP.10: If the axe is dull and he does not sharpen its edge, then he must exert more strength; but wisdom [to sharpen the axe] helps him succeed [with less effort].
AMP.11: If the serpent bites before being charmed, then there is no profit for the charmer.
AMP.12: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious and win him favor, but the lips of a fool consume him;
AMP.13: the beginning of his talking is foolishness and the end of his talk is wicked madness.
AMP.14: Yet the fool multiplies words, though no man knows what will happen, and who can tell him what will come after he is gone?
AMP.15: The labor of a fool so wearies him [because he is ignorant] that he does not even know how to go to a city.
AMP.16: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child and when your [incompetent] officials and princes feast in the morning.
AMP.17: Blessed [prosperous and admired] are you, O land, when your king is a man of noble birth, and your princes and officials feast at the proper time—for strength and not for drunkenness.
AMP.18: Through laziness the rafters [of state affairs] decay and the roof sags, and through idleness [the roof of] the house leaks.
AMP.19: The officials make a feast for enjoyment [instead of repairing what is broken], and serve wine to make life merry, and money is the answer to everything.
AMP.20: Moreover, do not curse the king, even in your bedroom, and in your sleeping rooms do not curse the rich, for a bird of the air will carry the sound and a winged creature will make the matter known.

MSG.1:
Dead flies in perfume make it stink,
And a little foolishness decomposes much wisdom.
MSG.2:
Wise thinking leads to right living;
Stupid thinking leads to wrong living.
MSG.3:
Fools on the road have no sense of direction.
The way they walk tells the story: "There goes the fool again!"
MSG.4:
If a ruler loses his temper against you, don't panic;
A calm disposition quiets intemperate rage.
MSG.5:
Here's a piece of bad business I've seen on this earth,
An error that can be blamed on whoever is in charge:
MSG.6:
Immaturity is given a place of prominence,
While maturity is made to take a back seat.
MSG.7:
I've seen unproven upstarts riding in style,
While experienced veterans are put out to pasture.
MSG.8:
Caution: The trap you set might catch you.
Warning: Your accomplice in crime might double-cross you.
MSG.9:
Safety first: Quarrying stones is dangerous.
Be alert: Felling trees is hazardous.
MSG.10:
Remember: The duller the ax the harder the work;
Use your head: The more brains, the less muscle.
MSG.11:
If the snake bites before it's been charmed,
What's the point in then sending for the charmer?
MSG.12:
The words of a wise person are gracious.
The talk of a fool self-destructs—
MSG.13:
He starts out talking nonsense
And ends up spouting insanity and evil.
MSG.14:
Fools talk way too much,
Chattering stuff they know nothing about.
MSG.15:
A decent day's work so fatigues fools
That they can't find their way back to town.
MSG.16:
Unlucky the land whose king is a young pup,
And whose princes party all night.
MSG.17:
Lucky the land whose king is mature,
Where the princes behave themselves
And don't drink themselves silly.
MSG.18:
A shiftless man lives in a tumbledown shack;
A lazy woman ends up with a leaky roof.
MSG.19:
Laughter and bread go together,
And wine gives sparkle to life—
But it's money that makes the world go around.
MSG.20:
Don't bad-mouth your leaders, not even under your breath,
And don't abuse your betters, even in the privacy of your home.
Loose talk has a way of getting picked up and spread around.
Little birds drop the crumbs of your gossip far and wide.

NRSVCE.4:
If the anger of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your post,
for calmness will undo great offenses.
NRSVCE.5: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as great an error as if it proceeded from the ruler:
NRSVCE.6: folly is set in many high places, and the rich sit in a low place.
NRSVCE.7: I have seen slaves on horseback, and princes walking on foot like slaves.
NRSVCE.8:
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it;
and whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a snake.
NRSVCE.9:
Whoever quarries stones will be hurt by them;
and whoever splits logs will be endangered by them.
NRSVCE.10:
If the iron is blunt, and one does not whet the edge,
then more strength must be exerted;
but wisdom helps one to succeed.
NRSVCE.11:
If the snake bites before it is charmed,
there is no advantage in a charmer.
NRSVCE.12:
Words spoken by the wise bring them favor,
but the lips of fools consume them.
NRSVCE.13:
The words of their mouths begin in foolishness,
and their talk ends in wicked madness;
NRSVCE.14:
yet fools talk on and on.
No one knows what is to happen,
and who can tell anyone what the future holds?
NRSVCE.15:
The toil of fools wears them out,
for they do not even know the way to town.
NRSVCE.16:
Alas for you, O land, when your king is a servant,
and your princes feast in the morning!
NRSVCE.17:
Happy are you, O land, when your king is a nobleman,
and your princes feast at the proper time —
for strength, and not for drunkenness!
NRSVCE.18:
Through sloth the roof sinks in,
and through indolence the house leaks.
NRSVCE.19:
Feasts are made for laughter;
wine gladdens life,
and money meets every need.
NRSVCE.20:
Do not curse the king, even in your thoughts,
or curse the rich, even in your bedroom;
for a bird of the air may carry your voice,
or some winged creature tell the matter.

NET.1: One dead fly makes the perfumer’s ointment give off a rancid stench, so a little folly can outweigh much wisdom.
NET.2: A wise person’s good sense protects him, but a fool’s lack of sense leaves him vulnerable.
NET.3: Even when a fool walks along the road he lacks sense, and shows everyone what a fool he is.
NET.4: If the anger of the ruler flares up against you, do not resign from your position, for a calm response can undo great offenses.
NET.5: I have seen another misfortune on the earth: It is an error a ruler makes.
NET.6: Fools are placed in many positions of authority, while wealthy men sit in lowly positions.
NET.7: I have seen slaves on horseback and princes walking on foot like slaves.
NET.8: One who digs a pit may fall into it, and one who breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
NET.9: One who quarries stones may be injured by them; one who splits logs may be endangered by them.
NET.10: If an iron axhead is blunt and a workman does not sharpen its edge, he must exert a great deal of effort; so wisdom has the advantage of giving success.
NET.11: If the snake should bite before it is charmed, the snake charmer is in trouble.
NET.12: The words of a wise person win him favor, but the words of a fool are self-destructive.
NET.13: At the beginning his words are foolish and at the end his talk is wicked madness,
NET.14: yet a fool keeps on babbling. No one knows what will happen; who can tell him what will happen in the future?
NET.15: The toil of a stupid fool wears him out, because he does not even know the way to the city.
NET.16: Woe to you, O land, when your king is childish, and your princes feast in the morning!
NET.17: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobility, and your princes feast at the proper time — with self-control and not in drunkenness.
NET.18: Because of laziness the roof caves in, and because of idle hands the house leaks.
NET.19: Feasts are made for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.
NET.20: Do not curse a king even in your thoughts, and do not curse the rich while in your bedroom; for a bird might report what you are thinking, or some winged creature might repeat your words.
